newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures rally on U.S. consumer price data.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures rally on U.S. consumer price data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were higher early as buyers rushed in the pits before and after the release of the U.S. June Consumer Price Index, traders said.
They said the continued buying interest from Tuesday's close was a sign that September T-bonds may probe resistance at 114-22/32 to 114-24/32 before the close.

The contract rose to 114-12/32, below the seven-month high of 114-15/32, in reaction to U.S. CPI which rose 0.1 percent overall and in the core rate. Traders, on average, were looking for both rates to rise 0.2 percent, versus up 0.1 percent in the May CPI and up 0.2 percent in May's core CPI.

U.S. May business inventories were up 0.2 percent, compared to forecasts for up 0.3 percent, and sales fell 0.5 percent for the largest monthly decline since June 1996, the U.S. Commerce department said.
The reports supported growing market ideas that U.S. price pressures were weakening, traders and analysts said.

One pit broker bought about 3,000 September T-bonds after the data were released. One Japanese-based firm bought 1,500 contracts on the numbers after buying about 2,000 soon after the opening bell, traders said. September immediately shot up to Monday's high of 114-07/32.
Traders said the buying momentum was petering out ahead of the U.S. June industrial production and capacity utilization data at 0915 EDT/1315 GMT.
Production is seen rising 0.2 percent, compared to up 0.4 percent in May, and utilization is expected to fall slightly to 83.6 percent, from 83.7 percent in May.

Some traders said the 114-12/32 to 114-16/32 area, which currently equates to about 6.50 percent on the U.S. long bond yield, could be a formidable barrier to the near-term target of 114-24/32. The 114-22/32 to 114-24/32 area currently corresponds to a bond yield level of 6.46 to 6.45 percent.
"We could fall below the 6.50 percent level before we see a sustainable correction," John Kadich, T-bond futures floor analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc, said.
Kadich said a test of 114-24/32 could spark a rally to the 115-02/32 to 115-03/32 area in September T-bonds.
"We could hit 115-03/32 the way this market is acting," he said. "Even though we are overbought, the fundamentals are in control."
December Eurodollars rose to 94.07, with resistance at 94.10. Two U.S. firms each bought about several thousand of December before the production and use numbers, a trader said.

At 0810 CDT/1310 GMT, September T-bonds were 10/32 higher at 114-08/32, 10-year notes were up 05/32 at 109-19/32, and December Eurodollars were up 0.02 basis points at 94.06. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
